```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(gtsummary)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Load anonymized dataset
df <- read_csv(
  here::here("data", "clean_analysis_data.csv"),
  locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Standardize groups
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Group = case_when(
      str_detect(Group, "(?i)trainer|coach") ~ "Coach",
      str_detect(Group, "(?i)athlete") ~ "WR Athlete",
      TRUE ~ Group
    ),
    Group = factor(Group, levels = c("WR Athlete", "Coach"))
  )

# Reorder sport classes
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    C2_Classification = factor(C2_Classification,
                               levels = c("T33", "T34",
                                          "T52", "T53", "T54"))
  )

# Create Eligible Impairment
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Eligible_Impairment = case_when(
      C2_Classification %in% c("T33", "T34")                          ~ "Hypertonia / Ataxia / Athetosis",
      C2_Classification %in% c("T52", "T53", "T54") &
        C4_Impairment_ICD %in% c("Amputation",
                                  "Congenital malformations")         ~ "Limb Deficiency",
      C2_Classification %in% c("T52", "T53", "T54")                  ~ "Impaired Muscle Power",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Create Distance Group
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Distance_Group = case_when(
      str_detect(C3_Distance, "5000m|10000m|Maratona|Meia Maratona") ~ "Long-distance (≥5000m)",
      str_detect(C3_Distance, "800m|1500m")                          ~ "Middle-distance (800–1500m)",
      TRUE                                                            ~ "Sprint (100–400m)"
    )
  )

# Remove "Other" from technology
df <- df %>%
  mutate(C12_Tech_Available = na_if(C12_Tech_Available, "Other"))

df_athletes <- df %>% filter(Group == "WR Athlete")
df_coaches  <- df %>% filter(Group == "Coach")
```

---

## Overview / Visão Geral

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
This report presents the main findings of a cross-sectional survey investigating training practices, knowledge sources, and challenges among Brazilian elite wheelchair racing (WR) athletes and coaches. Data were collected during the **2025 Brazilian Paralympic Athletics Championship**.

The fully anonymized dataset and analysis scripts are available at:  
🔗 [GitHub](https://github.com/antunesdiego/wheelchair_racing_survey) · [OSF](https://osf.io/79yqp)
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
Este relatório apresenta os principais achados de um levantamento transversal sobre práticas de treinamento, fontes de conhecimento e desafios entre atletas e treinadores brasileiros de elite em corrida em cadeira de rodas. Os dados foram coletados durante o **Campeonato Brasileiro Paralímpico de Atletismo 2025**.

O conjunto de dados anonimizados e os scripts de análise estão disponíveis em:  
🔗 [GitHub](https://github.com/antunesdiego/wheelchair_racing_survey) · [OSF](https://osf.io/79yqp)
:::
:::

---

## Sample / Amostra

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
A total of **`r nrow(df_athletes)` athletes** and **`r nrow(df_coaches)` coaches** participated in this study, representing **66.6% of the total elite WR population** competing at the national level in Brazil (2025).
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
Um total de **`r nrow(df_athletes)` atletas** e **`r nrow(df_coaches)` treinadores** participaram deste estudo, representando **66,6% da população elite** de corrida em cadeira competindo em nível nacional no Brasil (2025).
:::
:::

## Table 1 — General Characteristics / Características Gerais {#sec-table1}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
Table 1 summarizes the demographic and competitive profiles of athletes and coaches, including gender, age, experience, educational background, competitive level, and perceived S&C effectiveness.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
A Tabela 1 resume os perfis demográficos e competitivos de atletas e treinadores, incluindo gênero, idade, experiência, formação educacional, nível competitivo e percepção sobre a efetividade do T&C.
:::
:::

```{r table1}
df_t1 <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Raw_Effectiveness = coalesce(D3_Prog_Effectiveness, D4_Effectiveness),
    Raw_Effectiveness = str_squish(Raw_Effectiveness),
    Effectiveness = case_when(
      str_detect(Raw_Effectiveness, "(?i)not ef")     ~ "Not effective",
      str_detect(Raw_Effectiveness, "(?i)very ef")    ~ "Very effective",
      str_detect(Raw_Effectiveness, "(?i)moderately") ~ "Moderately effective",
      str_detect(Raw_Effectiveness, "(?i)slightly")   ~ "Slightly effective",
      str_detect(Raw_Effectiveness, "(?i)^effective") ~ "Effective",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Effectiveness = factor(Effectiveness, levels = c(
      "Not effective", "Slightly effective",
      "Moderately effective", "Effective", "Very effective"
    )),
    Gender     = factor(B1_Gender, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Comp_Level = factor(Comp_Level, levels = c(
      "Local", "State", "Regional", "National", "International"
    )),
    Education = factor(C1_Education, levels = c(
      "Elementary School", "Technical School", "High School",
      "Bachelor's Degree", "Specialization", "Master's Degree"
    ))
  )

df_t1 %>%
  select(Group, Gender, B2_Age, B3_Experience_Years,
         Education, Comp_Level, Effectiveness) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = Group,
    label = list(
      Gender              ~ "Gender / Gênero",
      B2_Age              ~ "Age, years / Idade (anos)",
      B3_Experience_Years ~ "Experience, years / Experiência (anos)",
      Education           ~ "Educational Background / Formação",
      Comp_Level          ~ "Competitive Level / Nível Competitivo",
      Effectiveness       ~ "Perceived S&C Effectiveness / Efetividade Percebida do T&C"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous()  ~ "{mean} ± {sd}",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
    ),
    missing = "no"
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  modify_header(label = "**Characteristic / Característica**") %>%
  as_kable_extra(booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE, font_size = 11)
```

## Table 2 — Athlete Sport Profile / Perfil Esportivo dos Atletas {#sec-table2}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
Table 2 details the sport classification, impairment type, event distances, training supervision, equipment, and technology access of WR athletes.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
A Tabela 2 detalha a classificação esportiva, tipo de deficiência, distâncias de prova, supervisão do treinamento, equipamentos e acesso à tecnologia dos atletas.
:::
:::

```{r table2}
df_athletes %>%
  mutate(
    Eligible_Impairment = factor(Eligible_Impairment,
                                 levels = c("Impaired Muscle Power",
                                            "Limb Deficiency",
                                            "Hypertonia / Ataxia / Athetosis")),
    Prescriber   = factor(C6_Prescriber),
    Chair_Origin = factor(C8_Chair_Origin,
                          levels = c("Customized", "Collective use")),
    Maintenance  = factor(C7_Maintenance,
                          levels = c("By myself", "Coach/Professional")),
    Glove_Type   = factor(C9_Glove_Type),
    Wheel_Type   = factor(C10_Wheel_Type),
    Roller       = factor(C11_Roller_Available, levels = c("Yes","No"))
  ) %>%
  select(C2_Classification, C4_Impairment_ICD, Eligible_Impairment,
         Distance_Group, Prescriber, Chair_Origin, Maintenance,
         Glove_Type, Wheel_Type, Roller) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    label = list(
      C2_Classification   ~ "Sport Class / Classe Esportiva",
      C4_Impairment_ICD   ~ "Underlying Health Condition / Condição de Saúde",
      Eligible_Impairment ~ "Eligible Impairment / Deficiência Elegível (World Para Athletics)",
      Distance_Group      ~ "Event Distance Profile / Perfil de Distância",
      Prescriber          ~ "Training Prescriber / Prescritor do Treinamento",
      Chair_Origin        ~ "Racing Chair Origin / Origem da Cadeira",
      Maintenance         ~ "WR Maintenance / Manutenção da Cadeira",
      Glove_Type          ~ "Glove Type / Tipo de Luva",
      Wheel_Type          ~ "Wheel Type / Tipo de Roda",
      Roller              ~ "Access to Rollers / Acesso a Rolo"
    ),
    statistic = list(all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"),
    missing = "no"
  ) %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  modify_header(label = "**Athlete Characteristic / Característica do Atleta**") %>%
  as_kable_extra(booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE, font_size = 11)
```

## Table 3 — Coach Profiles and Monitoring / Perfil dos Treinadores e Monitoramento {#sec-table3}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
Table 3 presents the professional profiles of coaches, including their roles, national certification level, S&C information search frequency, S&C prescriber, and load monitoring methods.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
A Tabela 3 apresenta os perfis profissionais dos treinadores, incluindo funções, nível de certificação nacional, frequência de busca de informações sobre T&C, prescritor do T&C e métodos de monitoramento de carga.
:::
:::

```{r table3}
table3 <- tribble(
  ~Characteristic,                                                    ~n,          ~pct,
  "**Role in the Team / Função na Equipe**",                          NA_integer_, NA_character_,
  "Head Coach",                                                       14L,         "88%",
  "Assistant Coach",                                                   1L,         "6.3%",
  "Strength and Conditioning Coach",                                   1L,         "6.3%",
  "**National Certification Level (Level 1–3)**",                     NA_integer_, NA_character_,
  "Level 1 (introductory)",                                            3L,         "19%",
  "Level 2 (intermediate)",                                            5L,         "31%",
  "Level 3 (advanced)",                                                8L,         "50%",
  "**Frequency of S&C Information Search / Frequência de Busca**",   NA_integer_, NA_character_,
  "Never / Nunca",                                                     0L,         "0%",
  "Rarely / Raramente",                                                0L,         "0%",
  "Sometimes / Às vezes",                                              3L,         "19%",
  "Commonly / Frequentemente",                                         9L,         "56%",
  "Always / Sempre",                                                   4L,         "25%",
  "**Who Prescribes S&C / Quem Prescreve o T&C**",                   NA_integer_, NA_character_,
  "Coach / Treinador",                                                13L,         "81%",
  "S&C Coach / Especialista em T&C",                                   3L,         "19%",
  "**Load Monitoring — Performance Execution**",                      NA_integer_, NA_character_,
  "Isometric Strength",                                                4L,         "25%",
  "Coordination and Motor Test",                                       3L,         "19%",
  "Plyometric with Arms",                                              2L,         "13%",
  "GPS Device (Speed)",                                                2L,         "13%",
  "**Load Monitoring — Performance Outcome**",                        NA_integer_, NA_character_,
  "Rate of Perceived Exertion (RPE)",                                 11L,         "69%",
  "Training Session Time",                                            11L,         "69%",
  "Performance Test with Ballistic Exercises",                         8L,         "50%",
  "Speed",                                                             7L,         "44%",
  "Distance",                                                          5L,         "31%",
  "Heart Rate",                                                        4L,         "25%",
  "% of Competitive Performance",                                      4L,         "25%"
)

table3 %>%
  mutate(
    n   = ifelse(is.na(n),   "", as.character(n)),
    pct = ifelse(is.na(pct), "", pct)
  ) %>%
  kable(
    col.names = c("Characteristic / Característica", "n", "%"),
    booktabs  = TRUE,
    align     = c("l","c","c")
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE, font_size = 11) %>%
  row_spec(which(is.na(as.integer(table3$n))), bold = TRUE, background = "#f5f5f5") %>%
  footnote(
    general       = "N = 16 coaches; Level 1 = introductory, Level 2 = intermediate, Level 3 = advanced certification (Brazilian Paralympic Committee). Load monitoring: multiple responses allowed / respostas múltiplas permitidas.",
    general_title = ""
  )
```

## Key Findings / Principais Achados

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**1. Bench Press as cornerstone**  
The Bench Press was the most cited strength exercise by both athletes and coaches across multiple training categories.

**2. Role overload**  
Most coaches simultaneously manage technical training, S&C programming, and equipment maintenance — with only 3 coaches reporting a dedicated S&C specialist.

**3. Technological gap**  
While coaches aspire to integrate AI, IMU sensors, and power meters, athletes remain primarily concerned with basic accessibility and infrastructure.

**4. RPE as primary monitoring tool**  
Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE) was the most used monitoring method (69% of coaches), reflecting pragmatic adaptation to the limitations of conventional physiological monitoring in this population.

**5. Representative sample**  
The study captured 66.6% of the total elite WR population in Brazil, including 72.4% of male and 53.8% of female elite athletes.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**1. Supino como exercício central**  
O Supino foi o exercício de força mais citado por atletas e treinadores em múltiplas categorias de treinamento.

**2. Sobrecarga de funções**  
A maioria dos treinadores gerencia simultaneamente o treinamento técnico, a prescrição de T&C e a manutenção de equipamentos — com apenas 3 treinadores reportando um especialista dedicado em T&C.

**3. Lacuna tecnológica**  
Enquanto os treinadores aspiram integrar IA, sensores IMU e medidores de potência, os atletas permanecem principalmente preocupados com acessibilidade básica e infraestrutura.

**4. PSE como principal ferramenta de monitoramento**  
A Percepção Subjetiva de Esforço (PSE) foi o método de monitoramento mais utilizado (69% dos treinadores), refletindo adaptação pragmática às limitações do monitoramento fisiológico convencional nessa população.

**5. Amostra representativa**  
O estudo capturou 66,6% da população elite total de corrida em cadeira no Brasil, incluindo 72,4% dos atletas masculinos e 53,8% das atletas femininas de elite.
:::
:::
